kind: holder's official news release on its own commissioned radiocarbon test
title: Carbon dating finds Bakhshali manuscript contains oldest recorded origins of the symbol 'zero'
creator: Bodleian Libraries, University of Oxford (holder of MS. Sansk. d. 14, the Bakhshali manuscript)
access: live page now behind a Cloudflare check (not bypassed); Wayback copy of 30 Sep 2017 used
note: Author's interest: the Bodleian holds the manuscript, commissioned the test and was lending a folio to a Science Museum exhibition; a 'world's oldest' result raises the value of its holding. The underlying paper is 'available on request' and was not opened (lite cap). Treat dates as the holder's statement.

kind: medieval text in a printed critical edition (public domain)
title: Il Liber abbaci di Leonardo Pisano (Scritti di Leonardo Pisano, vol. 1), ed. Baldassarre Boncompagni
creator: Leonardo son of Bonacci of Pisa (text); B. Boncompagni (editor, Rome 1857)
created: text dated 1202 in its incipit; edition 1857
access: archive.org OCR text (Google scan); OCR has letter errors, quotes copied as OCR prints them
note: Author's interest: Leonardo is selling his book's method as better than every rival ('algorismus', Pythagoras's arcs); crediting the Indians costs him nothing and dignifies the method. The edition prints the revised text dedicated to Michael Scot; the incipit gives 1202.

kind: medieval Latin text in a printed edition (public domain)
title: Algoritmi de numero indorum, in Trattati d'aritmetica, ed. Baldassarre Boncompagni (Rome 1857), I
creator: Latin version of al-Khwarizmi's arithmetic ('Dixit algoritmi'); edited from Cambridge University Library MS Ii.6.5, ff.102r-109v
created: medieval manuscript (date not stated in this source); edition 1857
origin: al-Khwarizmi via an unnamed Latin translator
note: Author's interest: a teaching text; it credits the Indians and even allows that they may have had reasons other than his own. The title 'Algoritmi de numero indorum' is Boncompagni's heading built from the opening words; the manuscript itself begins 'Dixit algoritmi'.
